tldr: Apple's Private Cloud Compute has run only on Apple-owned hardware since it launched. Google Cloud's June 23 confidential-computing update was the first public sign that was changing, naming Apple as an early customer for a new layered trust stack.
whats_new: Apple confirmed at WWDC that Private Cloud Compute now runs on Google Cloud — its first deployment outside Apple's own data centers — to handle agentic tool use and complex reasoning that on-device models can't cover.
why_it_matters: The deployment's three-layer trust stack — NVIDIA Blackwell confidential computing, Intel TDX, and Google's Titan chip as root of trust — is now a productized Google Cloud pattern (Confidential G4 VMs, open-source Prompt Encryption SDKs) any platform team can adopt instead of building attestation from scratch.

status.detail: PCC runs on Google Cloud using NVIDIA Blackwell confidential computing, Intel TDX, and Google's Titan chip as trust layers, built on a January 2026 multi-year Apple-Google agreement.

beats.headline: Google Cloud details the confidential-computing stack behind the deployment
beats.summary: Google's rollout post covers Confidential G4 VMs, open-source Prompt Encryption SDKs, and an Intel TDX/NVIDIA Blackwell/Titan chip trust layering — and names Apple Private Cloud Compute as the customer.

beats.headline: Apple confirms PCC's first deployment outside its own data centers
beats.summary: Apple's WWDC disclosure describes the same layered stack, built on a January 2026 multi-year Apple-Google agreement covering AI models and cloud infrastructure.

open_questions: Will Apple extend Private Cloud Compute to other cloud providers beyond Google Cloud?
Does the multi-year Apple-Google agreement also cover model training, or only inference?
take_for_builders: Evaluate Google Cloud's Confidential G4 VMs and open-source Prompt Encryption SDK before building your own TEE/attestation stack for encrypted, verifiable inference on someone else's cloud.
